partnershipPlan: Two patient partners review the removal explanation leaflet; each ward champion runs a short staff feedback round after mapping; urology reviews the reinsertion rules.
socialListening: No social media listening; patient comments from the four hospitals' feedback systems in the last year are searched for mentions of catheters.

items.theme: Nobody knew why it was there
items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I kept asking why I still had the tube, and every nurse said the doctor would decide.
items.implication: Nurse-driven removal needs visible authority at the bedside and a documented indication.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: If I take it out at night and he cannot pass urine, I am the one putting a new one in at four in the morning.
items.implication: Pair removal with a bladder scan rule and report reinsertion as a balancing measure.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: They arrive from theatre with a catheter and no plan, and after two shift changes nobody remembers why.
items.implication: Map the theatre handoff first and add the indication to the transfer note.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: They left it in because Mum was wet at night, but she hated it and it made her confused.
items.implication: Address incontinence care as part of standard work, not as a reason to keep a catheter.

summary: Four composite voices on authority, reinsertion, theatre handoffs and incontinence.
